External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar visited Kyiv for his first-ever bilateral trip to Ukraine, reiterating India's commitment to peace and offering assistance to end the conflict, emphasizing dialogue and diplomacy. The Allahabad High Court quashed the National Security Act (NSA) detention of Akriti Chaudhary, a student arrested during the Noida workers' protest, calling it "arbitrary" and ordering the government to pay her ₹5 lakh in compensation. Floods have spread across 31 districts in Uttar Pradesh, affecting 14,000 people in Chitrakoot alone, with thousands more evacuated. The Supreme Court sought an explanation from the Union Home Secretary regarding the implementation of its May 2025 judgment to reduce the deputation of Indian Police Service (IPS) officers to senior posts in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs). India is set to host the inaugural Women's Champions Trophy 2027, with the International Cricket Council (ICC) moving the six-team event from Sri Lanka to Mumbai and Vadodara, scheduled from February 14 to 28. The CBI is slated to probe the death case of Sushant Singh Rajput's ex-manager, Disha Salian.

---

Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has removed Konda Surekha, the State Minister for Environment, Forests and Endowments, from the Council of Ministers with immediate effect, following a controversy where her daughter, Konda Sushmita, made public remarks against CM Revanth Reddy on August 19, 2026. Concurrently, the Chief Minister withdrew G. Chinna Reddy's appointment as Vice Chairman of the Telangana State Planning Board and appointed Gadwal Vijayalakshmi to the position. Nerella Sharada was also approved as Chairperson of the Telangana State Commission for Women. As many as 123 teachers and faculty members from various education sectors in Telangana have been selected for the State Teacher Awards 2026, with three officials, including A Sridevasena and Kumar Deepak, also chosen for excellence awards, scheduled for presentation on September 5. Former minister and BRS deputy floor leader Talasani Srinivas Yadav warned of gheraoing Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy's residence if GO 97 is not withdrawn by September 7, as polytechnic students are protesting against the GO, which they believe threatens their future by potentially privatizing colleges. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at multiple locations in Telangana as part of a major crackdown on eight narcotics-related cases across southern states, an operation linked to the national Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan initiative, with searches in Telangana related to FIRs against Kalapathi Nithu Bai and others, focusing on an organized syndicate procuring and selling ganja.

---

The Andhra Pradesh government revoked the suspension of two senior IPS officers, Kanthi Rana Tata and Vishal Gunni, nearly two years after their initial suspension for alleged involvement in harassing a Mumbai-based actor-cum-model. Andhra Pradesh's literacy rate has increased significantly from 72.6% in 2024 to 82.1% in 2026, with approximately 25 lakh people becoming literate under the state government's Akshara Andhra programme, with the government aiming to achieve 100% literacy by September 2027. A seven-year-old girl died and 52 people, including 47 children, fell ill after receiving chloroquine tablets at a medical camp in Gollaguppa village, Polavaram district; the exact cause is under investigation, against a backdrop of historical malaria concerns in tribal areas of Andhra Pradesh.

section: ## SECTION 18 — Deep Analysis of Most Important Breaking News
content:
**What Happened:** External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar made his first-ever bilateral visit to Kyiv, Ukraine, where he reiterated India's commitment to peace and offered assistance to help end the ongoing Ukraine-Russia conflict.
**Root Causes:** The primary root cause is the prolonged conflict between Ukraine and Russia, which has significantly impacted regional and global geopolitics. India's stance stems from its long-standing foreign policy principles of non-alignment and emphasis on peaceful resolution of disputes.
**Historical Background:** India has maintained diplomatic relations with both Ukraine and Russia throughout the conflict, advocating for dialogue and diplomacy as the only viable path to peace. Prime Minister Modi has previously stated that "this is not an era of war," setting a tone for India's diplomatic engagements.
**Key Actors:** Key actors include India, represented by EAM S. Jaishankar; Ukraine, as the host nation; and Russia, as the other party to the conflict. International bodies and other nations also play roles in broader diplomatic efforts.
**Strategic Importance:** Jaishankar's visit is strategically important as it signals India's active diplomatic engagement in a major global conflict, positioning India as a potential mediator or facilitator of peace discussions. It also underscores India's independent foreign policy.
**Possible Long-Term Consequences:** This visit could potentially enhance India's diplomatic influence on the global stage and contribute to broader international efforts towards de-escalation. It may also shape future bilateral relations and humanitarian aid initiatives.
